To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The best adaptive strategy is the one that adjusts the transaction site affinity to compensate for the effect of obsolescence; (2) The best nonadaptive strategy is the one which is based on a weighted average of transaction site affinity and the current site utilization; and (3) A simple heuristic that is based on the current site utilization is the best nonadaptive strategy.

the adaptive strategies that take into consideration site affinity are superior to those that do not, and that the best adaptive strategy is the one that takes the most information into consideration.

a) a simple strategy that uses a single site as a backup to another site performs poorly in a distributed database environment, and b) the best strategy for selecting a site to process a transaction is to use a regression-based adaptive algorithm that adjusts for the effect of site affinity and information obsolescence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a distributed database management system (DDMS) that is robust to unreliable state information.
the problem of how to make load sharing decisions in an environment where the state information on which those decisions are based is subject to obsolescence.
the development and evaluation of load sharing strategies for use in distributed database systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best regression-based strategy is the one which considers transaction affinity in its regression equation.
a regression strategy that takes site affinity into consideration is the most appropriate load sharing strategy in a distributed system with unreliable state information.
the regression-based adaptive strategies are superior to the nonadaptive strategies, and that the regression strategies are more robust than the other adaptive strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adaptive strategies are more robust to the effects of information obsolescense than the non-adaptive strategies.
the best regression strategy (R1) is a good compromise between the best fixed strategy (FS2) and the best adaptive strategy without site affinity (A2).
we have examined a set of load balancing strategies that can be used to select sites for processing incoming transactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the use of a simple regression-based approach to adapt the selection of sites is a viable alternative to more sophisticated methods, the choice of the regression parameters is critical.
it is possible to design adaptive load sharing strategies that can be used in a distributed environment where sites may have unreliable or incomplete knowledge of the state of the system.
a simple adaptive strategy that considers transaction site affinity can perform as well as a strategy that uses a complex model of the underlying system.
